source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 26. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Moderate pace, both shoes, courtesy on the way

learn.en: When you leave home, say salam to your family and the du'aa for going out.
learn.title: Leaving home
learn.ar: بِسْمِ اللهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ
learn.tr: Bismi-llāh, tawakkaltu ʿala-llāh, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh

learn.en: Walk upright and humbly — not too fast, not too slow, not showing off. Don't drag your feet or keep looking back.
learn.title: Walk well

learn.en: Wear both shoes or neither — never just one! Keep a pleasant face.
learn.title: Both shoes

learn.en: Don't shout across the road; go closer. Hold the door for someone behind you, and wait for someone hurrying to the lift.
learn.title: Courtesy on the way

learn.en: Use “Thank you”, “Excuse me”, “Sorry” and “Jazak-Allahu khayran” often. Say salam when you come home.
learn.title: Kind words

learn.en: “And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice.” (Qur'an 31:19)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

words.en: May Allah reward you with good

quiz.en: The lift is closing and someone is rushing to it. You…
opts: keep the door open for them

quiz.en: Mum helps you with homework. You…
opts: get angry if she makes a mistake
tell her to finish it herself

quiz.en: True or false? Shouting on the road is good manners.
True or false? I should not drag my feet while walking.

think.q: Next time you're out, can you hold a door open for someone?
think.a: A small act — and a big smile from them!

parents.summary: Walking manners: the leaving-home du'aa, a calm upright walk, both shoes, holding doors, kind words, and salam on returning.

try.en: May Allah reward you with good

parents.tip: Notice and praise him when he holds a door.
